chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.
ai.seo_question: What is the basis of Satan's authority over humans according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is not inherent or absolute but contingent upon human *ikhtiyar* (free will), specifically when believers voluntarily yield to his whispers. This hadith underscores the Shia theological principle that spiritual bondage is a result of conscious choice rather than divine decree, reinforcing the concept of *al-amr bayn al-amrayn* (the matter between the two matters). It serves as a foundational argument for human responsibility in the struggle against the ego and the devil.
